headline: 1.3 KILOMETRES OF COPPER-GOLD: Aldebaran Drills 1,339m at 0.45% CuEq at Altar — Q3 Resource Upgrade in Play
snippet: Aldebaran Resources reported May 21 infill drill results from the Altar copper-gold project in San Juan, Argentina, including a headline intercept of 1,339.3m at 0.45% CuEq — with a best zone of 500m grading 0.71% CuEq. Results support upgrading inferred blocks to measured and indicated ahead of a Q3 2026 resource estimate incorporating 40,000+ metres of new drilling.

headline: COPPER REVERSAL: Base Metal Jumps 2% to $6.09/lb as Iran Peace Signals and China Trade Resumption Hit Markets
snippet: Copper futures climbed to roughly $6.09/lb — a six-week high — as Trump signalled US-Iran negotiations were in final stages and China resumed broader trade flows, reversing the prior session's selloff. Analysts warn the move is geopolitics-driven rather than fundamentals-driven, but the swing is material for base metal mining equities after weeks of Iran-driven losses.

headline: LITHIUM MINE BACK: MinRes Restarts Bald Hill After 18-Month Suspension — First Spodumene Production Due July
snippet: Mineral Resources announced it is restarting its 100%-owned Bald Hill lithium mine in Western Australia, which was placed on care and maintenance in November 2024. Mining and crushing begin in June with first spodumene concentrate production targeted for July; once online MinRes will be the only company globally operating three hard-rock lithium mines simultaneously.

headline: Orezone Drills First Results at Casa Berardi — 16.10 g/t Au Over 6.7m and 6.47 g/t Au Over 21.5m in Quebec
snippet: Orezone Gold (TSX: ORE) released its first drill results from the recently acquired Casa Berardi mine in Quebec — best intercepts of 16.10 g/t gold over 6.7 metres and 6.47 g/t over 21.5 metres from the F160 zone, supporting planned pit expansions. Orezone plans 40,000–60,000m of exploration drilling at Casa Berardi in 2026, ramping to 80,000–100,000m/yr.

headline: Troilus West Rim: 2.92 g/t AuEQ Over 19m Near Quebec Pit — Analysts Flag Project as M&A Target
snippet: Troilus Mining expanded its West Rim zone at the copper-gold Troilus Project in northcentral Quebec, returning 2.92 g/t AuEQ over 19 metres — entirely outside the current resource and within 200 metres of the planned reserve pit. Mining.com and Northern Miner noted the drill pattern raises the project's attractiveness to potential acquirers.

headline: GDX UP 108% IN A YEAR: Gold Miners Are Finally Outrunning the Metal — and the Re-Rating May Not Be Done
snippet: The VanEck Gold Miners ETF has returned 108% year-over-year, dramatically outpacing gold's 37% gain as record margins flow through to earnings. Analysts argue the sector re-rating has further to run — with Agnico Eagle posting $1.7B net income at $4,861/oz in Q1 2026 and miners still trading at historically undemanding P/E multiples despite the run-up.

headline: Equinox Gold Acquires Orla Mining in $5.1B Deal — Combined $18.5B Company Targets 1.1M oz Annual Production
snippet: Equinox Gold signed a US$5.1 billion all-stock deal to acquire Orla Mining, creating a combined Americas-focused gold producer with an US$18.5 billion market cap and approximately 1.1 million ounces of expected annual production. The deal unites Equinox's multi-mine portfolio with Orla's high-margin Camino Rojo operation in Mexico.

headline: CHINA SILVER DEMAND: 790+ Tonnes Imported in Early 2026 — Solar and Industrial Buying Sustain Record Pace
snippet: China imported over 790 tonnes of silver in early 2026, driven by aggressive solar panel manufacturing, EV production, and electronic components demand. The pace sustains the structural supply-deficit thesis even as silver pulls back from May highs near $87, with the market expected to record its sixth consecutive annual shortfall at 46.3 million ounces.

headline: WHY GOLD STILL GOES TO $5,000: What Institutional Forecasters See That Retail Investors Miss
snippet: With gold consolidating near $4,500 after a 2026 peak near $5,500, multiple institutional forecasters — including Goldman Sachs at $5,400 by year-end — maintain bullish targets. The piece unpacks the structural drivers retail investors tend to underweight: central bank accumulation near 80 tonnes/month, fiscal instability, and the dollar's slow debasement.
